title: Logbook of Merer (Wadi al-Jarf papyri A and B)
summary: Papyri found in 2013 at Wadi al-Jarf on the Red Sea coast form the oldest archive known from Egypt. They include the logbook of Inspector Merer, whose crew of about 40 men shipped Tura limestone to the Great Pyramid site at Akhet-Khufu in the last known year of Khufu, an eyewitness record of the pyramid nearing completion.

uncertainty.note: The logbook is dated in Khufu's regnal years (July to November of the year after the 13th census, called Year 26), not in absolute years; the BCE year follows Khufu's reign end c. 2566 BC in the ministry chronology and is approximate.

as_recorded.calendar: Egyptian civil calendar, Khufu regnal count
as_recorded.value: Akhet I to Peret II (July to November) of the year after the 13th census of Cheops (Year 26)

where.modern_name: Great Pyramid, Giza (the work site); logbooks found at Wadi al-Jarf, Red Sea coast, Egypt
where.historical_name: Akhet-Khufu, the pyramid site, with the Tura quarries across the Nile, Old Kingdom Egypt

importance.justification: The oldest papyri found in Egypt and the only contemporary account of the labour behind the Great Pyramid.

reviewer_note: The point is the pyramid site. The route is Tura to Akhet-Khufu in day-by-day entries without calendar dates, so no path animation was written. Wadi al-Jarf is where the papyri were found, not a stop in the log.
